title: Drunk BMW driver granted BAIL after cyclist's death in Camps Bay
text:
Drunk BMW driver granted BAIL after cyclist’s death in Camps Bay
A collision in Camps Bay has renewed calls for accountability on SA’s roads after a motorist accused of killing a cyclist was granted bail.
A fatal collision in Camps Bay has renewed calls for greater accountability on South Africa’s roads after a motorist accused of killing a cyclist was released on bail following his appearance in the Cape Town Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday.
The 27-year-old man faces charges of culpable homicide, reckless and negligent driving, and driving under the influence in connection with the death of 41-year-old Idries Sheriff, a husband and father.
Popular route
Sheriff was killed on Tuesday morning while cycling along Victoria Road, a route popular with both local and visiting cyclists.
According to allegations presented to the court, a high-performance vehicle, reportedly travelling at speed, lost control, crossed into the oncoming lane and mounted the pavement before striking him head-on.
The accused was arrested shortly after the incident.
His release on R15 000 bail has drawn criticism from members of the cycling community and the public.
Cyclists gathered outside the court in a show of solidarity with Sheriff’s family, calling for justice and greater accountability for motorists, particularly in cases involving vulnerable road users.
Western Cape Premier Alan Winde, himself an avid cyclist, also weighed in on the matter, thanking cyclists and the Pedal Power Association (PPA) for supporting the family and advocating for road safety.
“Thank you to the cyclists and the Pedal Power Association for standing with Idries’ family,” Winde said in a social media post, adding his call for swift justice.
The case has been postponed to 22 April 2026, and investigations into the circumstances surrounding the crash are continuing.
The PPA has appointed an attorney to observe the case proceedings.
